candidates.title: Ben Davison & Lee Wylie - The dynamic duo (the feint game ft. Josh Taylor)
candidates.principle: Feinting creates openings and disrupts opponent's timing
candidates.oneLiner: Strong principle teaching on feinting with partner flow, but limited chunkability and self-regulation reduce full alignment.

candidates.title: Elite Boxing Methods of Attack ~ Created by Lee Wylie
candidates.principle: How to set up and execute attacks using feints, angles, and timing
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches attack principles through analysis and shadow drills, but lacks loopability, partner flow, and self-regulation — more of a lecture/demonstration than a self-sustaining drill.

candidates.title: Boxing Short Studies: The Art of Side-stepping (Angles)-Lee Wylie Reupload
candidates.principle: Creating angles through lateral footwork and side-stepping
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches angle creation through side-stepping with good principle embodiment, but is a solo study with limited loopability, no partner flow, and no self-regulation.

candidates.title: Curtis Harper and The Sixth Way of Attack (Lee Wylie parody)
candidates.principle: Setting up attacks by first occupying the opponent's attention (the 'sixth way' of attack in boxing: the attack that is set up by a previous action or feint)
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches a sophisticated principle of attack setup through a playful, partner-based drill that forces awareness of timing and deception, though it lacks strong self-regulation mechanics.

candidates.title: Getting boxers plums. EP8 What the hell is Jack Slack talking about?
candidates.principle: Creating and exploiting the plum (double-collar tie) position
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches a specific clinch entry principle with partner flow and consciousness-forcing, but lacks strong self-regulation and loopability for pure rhythm work.

candidates.title: Doubling Up is Still the Secret Sauce of Combination Punching
candidates.principle: Doubling up punches creates openings and disrupts opponent's rhythm
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches a clear principle through repetition and awareness, but lacks partner flow and self-regulation, and may lean toward mindless repetition without strong consciousness forcing.

candidates.title: Jack Slack's Ringcraft: The Art Of The Stance
candidates.principle: Stance is the foundation of all movement and defense in boxing
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches stance principles with awareness but is solo, non-looping, and lacks self-regulation or partner flow.

candidates.title: A Filthy Casual's Guide to Alex Pereira's Left Hook
candidates.principle: Setting up power shots by manipulating opponent's reactions and creating angles
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches a clear principle of setup and timing but is a solo shadow drill with no partner flow, loopability, or self-regulation — more of a conceptual breakdown than a repeatable drill.

candidates.title: A Filthy Casual's Guide to Petr Yan
candidates.drillName: Petr Yan's Rhythm Breaking and Feinting
candidates.principle: Breaking opponent's rhythm through feints and level changes
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches rhythm and feinting principles well but is a solo analysis video with no partner flow or self-regulation, limiting loopability and drill structure.

candidates.title: GGG -  How Powerful Drills Became KO's
candidates.principle: Transferring power from drills to knockouts through rhythm, timing, and pressure
candidates.oneLiner: Strong partner flow and rhythm agility, but leans on power output and lacks self-regulation or patience reward mechanics.

candidates.title: Naoya Inoue | How Monster Drills Became KO's
candidates.drillName: Inoue's pad work and counter drills
candidates.principle: Timing and counter-punching through rhythm disruption
candidates.oneLiner: Strong on rhythm, patience, and principle embodiment but lacks self-regulation and loopability for full alignment.

candidates.title: The Secret Defense of Boxing Greats That Will Change How You Fight
candidates.principle: Defense creates offense — slipping and countering as a single motion
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches a strong defensive principle through partner work, but may rely on coach guidance and lacks strong self-regulation or loopability.

candidates.title: The Most Brilliant Footwork in Boxing Explained
candidates.principle: Footwork as a system of angles and positioning
candidates.oneLiner: Explains footwork principles conceptually but is a long lecture/demo with no partner flow, loopability, or self-regulation, making it a partial match for the coach's taste.

candidates.title: How I Knock Fighters Out with the Left Hook | Liam Harrison Breakdown
candidates.principle: Setting up the left hook by drawing reactions and exploiting defensive habits
candidates.oneLiner: Teaches a specific setup principle with patience emphasis, but is a solo breakdown/analysis video with no loopable drill or partner flow, limiting alignment with the coach's taste.
